report_identity.report_title: San Miguel Brewery Hong Kong Ltd. Annual Report 2024
report_identity.unit: HK$'000 in original filing; amounts in this fact pack use absolute HKD unless noted

business_overview.one_sentence: The group manufactures and distributes bottled, canned and draught beers, with Hong Kong operations also leasing investment properties in Hong Kong.

segments.name: Hong Kong
segments.description: Manufacture and distribution of own brewed beer, distribution of imported beer in Hong Kong and overseas, and leasing of Hong Kong investment properties.

segments.name: Mainland China
segments.description: Manufacture and distribution of own brewed beer products in southern China and overseas.

business_overview.revenue_model: Revenue is invoiced value of beer products sold, net of discounts, returns, VAT and consumption tax; rental income from investment properties is reported in other net income.
business_notes: 2024 revenue was HK$711.157m, down from HK$741.619m in 2023.
Largest customer contributed HK$392.420m of revenue in 2024, above 10% of group revenue.
2024 loss from operations included HK$90.000m impairment losses of non-current assets.

profit_cash_conversion.assessment: Operating cash flow stayed positive in 2022-2024, and three-year operating free cash flow median was HK$48.519m. Reported earnings are volatile because 2024 included HK$90m non-current asset impairment and 2023 benefited from tax credits; main analysis uses cash flow after capex rather than reported net profit.

evidence.description: Consolidated income statement, financial position and cash flow statement.
Cash and bank balances, Mainland China cash, financing liabilities and lease cash flows.
Business segments, revenue, major customer and segment assets/liabilities.
PPE, investment properties, fair value and non-current asset impairment.
2022-2023 comparative income statement and cash flow data.

gaps: Annual report does not disclose cash by parent company versus each subsidiary; haircut assumes outside-Mainland cash is more accessible but still not fully parent-level cash.
No restricted cash line was identified in note 17; absence of a disclosed line is not proof that all operating cash is distributable, so necessary operating cash is deducted separately.
Maintenance versus growth capital expenditure is not precisely split; analysis uses recent purchase of property, plant and equipment as a conservative maintenance/reinvestment proxy.
